body_en: Civil Air Patrol (CAP) has ordered 21 new Cessna piston aircraft from Textron Aviation, destined to support its search and rescue, disaster response, training and youth programs across the United States.

Textron Aviation announced the order on October 21, 2026, and expects to complete deliveries during 2027. The order comprises seven Cessna Skyhawk 172s, 11 Cessna Skylane 182s, two Cessna Turbo Skylane T182Ts and one Cessna Turbo Stationair HD 206.
CAP, a nonprofit that serves as the official civilian auxiliary of the US Air Force, is already the world’s largest operator of Cessna aircraft, with a fleet of 543 single-engine planes.
Aircraft to support search and rescue, disaster response and youth programs
CAP’s 72,000 members, about 35,000 adults and 37,000 young cadets, operate from 1,424 locations nationwide.
Beyond emergency services, the organization supports military training and government agencies and runs aviation and STEM education programs for cadets, who can join up from the age of 12.

“These Cessna aircraft help ensure our members are ready when communities need us, whether searching for someone who is missing, responding after a disaster, or introducing young people to aviation,” said Major General Regena Aye, CAP’s national commander and CEO.

Since October 2024, CAP has flown nearly 200,000 hours, carried out 860 search and rescue missions and saved 104 lives, according to the organization. It claims to have saved nearly 5,000 lives since it began tracking in 1967.
CAP also reported that its work has delivered an estimated $334 million in operational value in 2025.

Frontier Airlines first class formally launches March 2027

For context, Frontier plans to reconfigure its entire fleet to add eight first class seats at the front of the cabin, with two rows of seats in a 2-2 configuration. Up until now, we haven’t known the timeline for this being introduced, though now we know. The expectation is that Frontier will start reconfiguring planes with first class as of late October 2026, and then seats will be on sale for travel as of March 5, 2027. So while the seats will already be in service, and some customers will luck out, that’s the formal launch plan.

The expectation is that all planes will have first class by then. That’s obviously a fast timeline, but keep in mind most of the cabin will remain unchanged, so it shouldn’t take much time to reconfigure each aircraft.

Hilton lets elite members redeem points with app check-out

Hilton Honors has launched Pay with Points. The idea is that elite members — Hilton Honors Silver, Gold, and Diamond members — can apply points toward eligible hotel charges during digital check-out in the Hilton Honors app.

This feature is now available at 150 participating hotels in the United States. This is expected to expand to more than 800 hotels by the end of 2026, with a full rollout to more than 6,000 properties in the US and Canada by early 2027. Availability and eligible redemption options may vary by property.

Hilton claims it’s the first major hotel brand to offer something like this through a fully digital check out experience with no front desk visit required. That’s true, though the point of differentiation here isn’t the ability to redeem points toward on-property spending, but instead, the ability to do this without interacting with someone at the front desk. Accor Live Limitless , Global Hotel Alliance , and World of Hyatt , all let you redeem points toward hotel costs at check-out.

body_en: United Airlines has just announced the opening of a new concourse at Houston George Bush Intercontinental Airport (IAH). In addition to adding gate capacity and having a modern design, it also has a cool amenity, in the form of the largest airline lounge in the Americas.
New 800-seat United Club Houston Terminal B North opens
The new Terminal B North Concourse at Houston Airport is open as of this week. The new concourse is three levels, 765,000 square feet, and has 22 mainline gates.

But perhaps what’s most exciting is that this concourse is home to a new 54,000 square foot United Club, making it the largest airline lounge in the United States, and for that matter, the largest in all of the Americas.

The new lounge has seating for 800 people, with a 1,350 square foot outdoor terrace, panoramic views of the airfield, two full service bars, two buffet stations, 11 private phone booths, and more. Here’s how the design is described:

Inspired by Houston’s distinctive spirit, the club’s design captures the feeling of traveling from the city to the sky, blending elements of the local cityscape and bayou landscape with nods to Houston’s legacy as a center of aerospace innovation and cultural diversity. The space features a curated collection of artwork from predominantly Texas-based artists, including photography by a San Antonio-based United employee.

body_en: Turkey has signed a long-anticipated £8 billion ($11 billion) deal to acquire Eurofighter Typhoons, the first major export contract for the four-nation combat aircraft since 2017. Twenty new-built aircraft will be purchased in the country’s first acquisition of a European combat aircraft after decades of operating new and secondhand U.S.-built fighters. But Turkey’s Eurofighter order could more than double in size, according to Turkish Defense Minister Yasar Guler. He declared that Ankara would also buy another 24 aircraft second hand, 12 each from Oman and Qatar. If those sales go through, Oman would be giving up Eurofighter operations. Included in the £5.4 billion are the aircraft and the weapons package from MBDA, including some integration work, potentially for Turkish indigenous weaponry. The remaining £2.6 billion is support and training activity, which will be contracted later, BAE Systems officials say. The deal was struck during a meeting between UK Prime Minister Keir Starmer and Turkish President Recep Tayyip Erdoğan in Ankara. Starmer said the deal was a win for British workers and the wider UK defense industry. Government officials claim the order is “saving the Warton production line,” after concerns about a lack of new orders for UK-built Typhoons were expressed by workers unions. UK industry has a 37% share in the Eurofighter program and production of major component assemblies is being ramped up thanks to orders from the other Eurofighter partner nations including Germany, Italy and Spain. “Today’s announcement extends Typhoon production and preserves crucial sovereign skills which underpin the UK’s defense and security,” BAE Systems CEO Charles Woodburn said. The deal is another major boost for the UK defense industry, coming just weeks after the UK’s Type 26 frigates were selected by Norway in a £10 billion deal. UK Defense Secretary John Healey said the deal went beyond the procurement of aircraft. “It is the leading edge of the growing defense and industrial partnership between our two nations,” he said. As part of the visit, Starmer also visited the facilities of Turkish Aerospace Industries, where he was shown the indigenous Kaan combat aircraft. He was also exposed to the Hurjet advanced jet trainer, a potential candidate to replace the BAE Systems Hawk jet trainer in the UK Royal Air Force (RAF) inventory. The deal follows three years of negotiations, which have included lobbying of the German government for Berlin to lift a restriction on a Eurofighter sale after Erdoğan’s government arrested Istanbul Mayor Ekrem İmamoğlu, who is seen as a serious presidential rival to Erdoğan in upcoming elections. The administration of German Chancellor Friedrich Merz lifted the sanctions in part because of the benefit to German industry. A memorandum of understanding between the UK and Turkish governments for a Eurofighter sale was agreed to in July. Turkey’s interest in the aircraft is driven in part by a need for a more capable air combat platform to be available in the interim until advanced versions of the Kaan aircraft are produced in the 2030s. Ankara’s decision to opt for a European fighter, meanwhile, will have been driven by a need to diversify sources of supply after facing sanctions from the U.S. over its purchase of a Russian air defense system and banishment from the F-35 Joint Strike Fighter program. The transfer of Omani and Qatari aircraft to Turkey begs questions over the future of additional Eurofighter orders from Qatar, which has long been linked to orders for a further 12 aircraft for a total of 36. Oman, meanwhile, appears to want to consolidate its fighter fleet around the Lockheed Martin F-16 Block 50. In BAE Systems’ 2023 full-year results, the company revealed that the Omani air force had chosen not to renew support arrangements for its Typhoons, and it is unclear how active that fleet now is. Buying these additional aircraft would mean Turkey would have a mix of three configurations in its fleet. Qatar’s aircraft have the Mk.0 version of the active electronically scanned array European Common Radar System (ECRS) radar, while Oman’s feature the mechanically scanned Captor sensor. In addition to the Eurofighter order, Erdoğan and Starmer also revealed they were working on a new trade and security pact.

body_en: The B-21 Raider program completed the first flight of a second airborne test aircraft in Palmdale, California on Sept. 11, clearing a key milestone a month before the 10th anniversary of the U.S. Air Force contract award to Northrop Grumman. Witnesses posted video on social media showing the B-21 flight-test aircraft passing overhead with wheels retracted and followed by a Lockheed Martin F-16 chase plane. “We can now expedite critical evaluations of mission systems and weapons capabilities, directly supporting the strategic deterrence and combat effectiveness envisioned for this aircraft,” Air Force Secretary Troy Meink said. Northrop assembles all B-21s inside Building 401 on Site 4 of the Air Force’s Plant 42 complex at Palmdale Regional Airport. New test aircraft must fly out of the public airport after they have been assembled, before they can relocate to the secure area of nearby Edwards Air Force Base. The milestone comes nearly 22 months after Northrop completed the maiden sortie of the first flight test version of the B-21 on Nov. 10, 2023. The company has also delivered to the Air Force two more fully assembled airframes, which are reserved for static and fatigue testing on the ground. Two more flight-test aircraft have been in some stage of assembly since at least February 2022. Air Force officials say the program remains on track to clear the initial operational capability milestone in the mid-2020s. Northrop won the $21.4 billion contract in October 2015 for the engineering and manufacturing development phase of the Long-Range Strike Bomber, which the Air Force later rechristened as the B-21 Raider. The Air Force also signed orders with Northrop for the first two-year lots of low-rate initial production.
body_zh: B-21 Raider 项目于 9 月 11 日在加利福尼亚州帕姆代尔完成了第二架机载测试机的首飞，在美国空军授予诺斯罗普·格鲁曼公司合同 10 周年前一个月实现了一个重要的里程碑。目击者在社交媒体上发布的视频显示，轮子收起的 B-21 试飞机从头顶飞过，后面跟着一架洛克希德·马丁公司的 F-16 追击机。空军部长特洛伊·梅克说：“我们现在可以加快对任务系统和武器能力的关键评估，直接支持这架飞机的战略威慑和战斗力。”诺斯罗普公司在帕姆代尔地区机场空军 42 号工厂 4 号基地的 401 号楼内组装所有 B-21。新的测试飞机必须在组装后飞离公共机场，然后才能转移到附近爱德华兹空军基地的安全区域。这一里程碑是在诺斯罗普公司于 2023 年 11 月 10 日完成 B-21 首次飞行测试版本的首次飞行近 22 个月后实现的。该公司还向空军交付了两架组装更齐全的机身，用于地面静态和疲劳测试。至少自 2022 年 2 月起，另外两架飞行测试飞机已进入组装阶段。空军官员表示，该计划仍在按计划进行，将在 2020 年代中期实现初始作战能力里程碑。诺斯罗普公司于 2015 年 10 月赢得了价值 214 亿美元的合同，用于远程攻击轰炸机的工程和制造开发阶段，空军后来将其重新命名为 B-21 袭击者。空军还与诺斯罗普公司签署了前两年批量低速初始生产的订单。

title_zh: 阿联酋航空将为您在迪拜度过的每一分钟提供一英里

summary_zh: 阿联酋航空Skywards会员每在迪拜消费一分钟可获得一英里奖励里程，但上限为7,200英里，五天后即可到达
body_en: Emirates Skywards has just launched a creative promotion. I love when loyalty programs think outside the box, and this is the perfect example of that. Now, whether people actually want to visit Dubai right now is a different question…
Emirates’ creative “mile-a-minute” promotion details
Thanks to a limited time promotion , Emirates is offering Skywards members one mile for every minute they spend in Dubai:
This is valid for tickets booked between October 21 and November 5, 2026
This is valid for travel between October 21 and December 13, 2026
All Skywards members are eligible, but registration is required
The ticket must originate outside the UAE, with the Dubai stay lasting between 24 hours and 30 days
The ticket must book a ticket directly through Emirates or flydubai, and must be for roundtrip travel
The ticket must be eligible to earn Skywards miles, meaning that award tickets don’t qualify

The calculated length of stay is based on the ticketed itinerary — you can either have an extended stopover in Dubai (like flying New York to Dubai to Delhi), or you can make Dubai your destination (like flying New York to Dubai to New York)

While Emirates is an independently profitable airline, there’s no denying that a major incentive for the carrier is also to build up the economy of Dubai, and that largely comes in the form of encouraging people to visit. Keep in mind that the carrier also has the “My Emirates Pass” concept , where your Emirates boarding pass can unlock savings at retailers throughout the UAE.
